_comment: Discord server-status bot (scripts/discord_status_bot.py).
Copy this file to config/discord_status_bot.json and fill in real values.
config/ is gitignored in full, so the copy you fill in never gets committed --
same arrangement webhooks.json already relies on. Keys starting with '_' are
ignored by the loader, which is why this block does not break it.
token         - the bot's token from the Discord Developer Portal
(Applications -> your app -> Bot -> Reset Token).
No privileged gateway intents are required: the bot only
sets its own presence and never reads messages or members.
game_host     - where DreamDaemon is listening. 127.0.0.1 if the bot runs
on the same box as the server.
game_port     - the game server's port, the same one players connect to.
poll_seconds  - how often to ask the server for status. Default 10.
Keep this BELOW the length of a full persistence save
(~18s) or the bot can step over a save entirely and only
notice it afterwards. The endpoint is cheap and exempt
from fail2topic, and presence is only pushed when
something actually changed, so 10s costs very little.
timeout_seconds        - how long to wait for the server to answer one
poll. BYOND is single-threaded and answers Topic on the
same thread that runs the persistence save, so this wants
headroom over a normal save. Default 10.
offline_after_failures - consecutive missed polls before the bot shows
'server offline'. Default 3. Until then it holds the last
known status, so a save that briefly blocks the world does
not flash a false offline. Lower it to 1 for the old
fail-immediately behaviour.
exit_after_offline_seconds - how long the server may be unreachable before
a SERVER-STARTED bot shuts itself down. Default 300 (5 min).
This exists because closing DreamDaemon directly, a taskkill
or a crash never runs the in-game shutdown hook, so the bot
would otherwise outlive its server forever. 300 is well past
how long a round restart takes, so restarts never trip it.
Set 0 to disable. Has NO effect on a hand-started bot.
SERVER-STARTED vs HAND-STARTED
scripts/discord_bot_start passes --managed. Only a --managed bot writes
data/discord_status_bot.pid, and that PID file is the ONLY thing the server
will ever stop or reap. Run the script yourself:
python scripts/discord_status_bot.py
and you get a bot with no PID file, no watchdog, and complete immunity from
the server stopping it -- so you can leave it up while the server is down.
Either kind takes data/discord_status_bot.lock, so the server will not start
a second bot next to one you already have running. In that case the SERVER's
bot exits; yours is never killed to make room.
The bot reads the get_serverstatus Topic command, which needs no auth key.
Nothing here is a secret except 'token' -- treat that like a password.
